title: bmc brewing
venue_description:
Bite My Cookies Brewing Company

bmc brewing is a family-owned and operated nanobrewery that opened in 2021 in the heart of The Plant complex in Pittsboro North Carolina. Founded by John and Carmen Rice the brewery represents more than 30 years of home brewing experience combined with John's background as a pharmaceutical researcher specializing in drug discovery cell biology and yeast physiology.

The Beer and Brewing Philosophy

The brewery features 18 taps of beer brewed on-site using ultra-purified reverse osmosis water and locally sourced ingredients. Grains come from Epiphany Craft Malt in Durham hops are grown at Bee Hoppy Farms in Chatham County and specialty ingredients like pumpkins sweet potatoes and coffee are sourced locally. The beer selection includes traditional styles like Mendel's Dominant Recessive Kolsch Buddy's Pale Ale Uisce Mona Stout and Cascades of Insanity IPA as well as seasonal and specialty brews. Many beers pay homage to acclaimed scientists and historical figures.

Music Events and Community Gathering

bmc brewing has established itself as a vital music venue in Chatham County hosting regular events that bring the community together. The Songwriter Open Mic takes place on the fourth Sunday of each month from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Hosted by Michael J. Brennan this acoustic event welcomes both original songs and covers with a maximum of two performers on stage at a time. Sign-up begins at 1:30 PM and the event is free to attend.

The venue also hosts Acoustic Jam sessions twice monthly - on the second and fourth Tuesdays from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM and on the second and fourth Thursdays from 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM. These casual gatherings invite musicians to bring their stringed instruments and collaborate in a relaxed brewery atmosphere.

The Plant and Chatham Beverage District

bmc brewing is part of The Plant a 17-acre complex that has become known as the Chatham Beverage District. Neighboring businesses include Starrlight Mead Fair Game Beverage Company Chatham Cider Works Copeland Springs Farm & Kitchen Hempsmith Oak City Hemp Carolina Hemp Tours Metal Brixx Cafe Pittsboro ebikes and Chatham Axes. The brewery building also houses the Smelt Art Gallery creating a unique intersection of craft beer and visual arts.

Sustainability and Community Focus

True to its name Bite My Cookies Brewing Company is committed to sustainability and community engagement. The brewery uses as much solar power as possible to run operations and processes spent grains into flour to create delicious cookies for customers - turning brewing byproducts into treats rather than waste. bmc brewing actively partners with local non-profits and creates jobs for folks who love craft beer and enjoy helping customers discover new styles.

Regular Events and Special Offerings

Beyond music events bmc brewing hosts a variety of weekly activities. Mondays feature Euchre nights paired with $5 pint specials. Tuesdays are Tequila Tuesdays with $1 off tequila drinks all day. Wednesdays showcase Whiskey Wednesdays with special whiskey tastings and flights. The venue also hosts game nights trivia special beer releases and collaborative events with other Plant tenants.

Venue Atmosphere and Amenities

The brewery offers both indoor taproom seating and outdoor patio space making it suitable for various weather conditions and preferences. The intimate setting is perfect for acoustic performances and casual jam sessions while still accommodating larger crowds for special events. The venue is family-friendly and welcomes people of all ages to enjoy the music food trucks and community atmosphere.

Awards and Recognition

bmc brewing has received recognition for its quality brews including a Silver medal at the 2022 NC Brewer's Cup for their Black Squirrel English Style Brown Porter with Coffee in the Field & Spiced Beer category.

title: Bynum Front Porch
venue_description:
Historic Community Gathering Place

Bynum Front Porch is a nonprofit organization that operates out of the historic Bynum General Store built in 1934. Located at 950 Bynum Road in Bynum North Carolina (part of Chatham County near Pittsboro and Siler City) this beloved community space has become one of the region's premier destinations for traditional music storytelling and cultural preservation.

The History of Bynum

Bynum was originally a cotton mill village set along the banks of the Haw River with the first mill built around 1872. As the mill grew the town flourished becoming a vibrant community where neighbors knew each other and children played along the riverbanks. At its peak Bynum had five stores two grist mills a movie theater and a school. The Bynum General Store opened in 1934 and served as the social center of the community.

When the mill closed in 1983 Bynum's community life began to change dramatically. The mill and school are long gone but the residents of Bynum remain vibrant and committed to preserving their community spirit. In 2001 neighbors created the Friday Night Music Series to help sustain the Bynum General Store and Post Office. By 2006 this effort formalized into Bynum Front Porch a nonprofit that leases the old general store and creates family-friendly events and programs that celebrate the community's rich history and bright future.

Bluegrass Jam Circle

The Bluegrass Jam Circle meets every second and fourth Saturday of the month from 10:00 AM until around noon. This open circle jam welcomes musicians of all skill levels and ages playing acoustic instruments only. Whether you pick or sing you're invited to bring your instrument or voice and join in making music at the historic Bynum General Store. The Circle Jam is free and open to the public and has become a beloved tradition for local bluegrass enthusiasts and those just discovering the genre.

Friday Night Music Series

Running from May through the end of August the Bynum Friday Night Music Series presents live performances every Friday from 7:00 PM to 8:30 PM. The series began in 2001 and features a diverse array of bands spanning multiple musical genres including gospel folk blues rockabilly and bluegrass. Performances typically take place on the outdoor stage weather permitting with the option to move inside the air-conditioned general store during inclement weather.

The events are free to attend with a hat passed for voluntary contributions to support the performers. Food vendors are typically on-site and parking is available at the Bynum ball field or in the adjacent field. The series has built a reputation for bringing quality regional and local talent to this intimate historic setting.

Mill Town Yarns Performance Series

Bynum Front Porch's Mill Town Yarns series has earned recognition from the NC Storytellers Guild as one of the state's premier storytelling hubs. This monthly performance series features top storytellers singer-songwriters and other performers who share their craft within the historic walls of the Bynum General Store. The 2025-26 season features a mix of professional and local performers creating intimate one-of-a-kind experiences.

Past performers have included nationally and internationally beloved artists such as Lipbone Redding Bil Lepp Michael Reno Harrell and Josh Goforth. The series also showcases local acoustic favorites NC professional storytellers and Chatham County stories and songs. Events typically take place at 7:00 PM with some shows free (donations welcome) and others ticketed depending on the performer.

Community Programs and Services

Over the years Bynum Front Porch has hosted Girl Scouts and Boy Scouts community picnics and offered the facility for rent to the wider Bynum community for birthday parties baby showers wedding receptions and other celebrations. The organization has also given over $30000 in grants to Chatham County students to continue their education demonstrating a deep commitment to supporting the next generation.

Additional programs include Bynum's Byte Night held every other Thursday from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM - a tech hangout for anyone curious about computers electronics or AI. The organization also hosts special events like community yard sales story slams and seasonal celebrations throughout the year.

The Venue Space

The Bynum General Store building maintains its historic character while serving as a versatile performance and gathering space. The interior can accommodate seated audiences for storytelling and concerts while the outdoor areas provide space for larger summer events. The building is located off Highway 15-501 making it accessible from Pittsboro Siler City Chapel Hill and other Triangle-area communities.

Impact on Regional Music Scene

Bynum Front Porch has become an essential part of the Chatham County and greater Triangle area music and cultural scene. By providing a regular venue for bluegrass jams traditional music performances and storytelling the organization helps preserve and promote North Carolina's rich musical heritage. The welcoming atmosphere and commitment to all skill levels makes it an ideal place for musicians to develop their craft connect with other players and share music with an appreciative audience.
